question: Which is the basic structural and functional unit of the nervous system?
solution:
The correct answer __**Neuron.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The basic unit of the nervous system is a nerve cell or neuron. The human brain contains about 100 billion neurons.**
 
• Neurons, or nerve cells, are the main structural and functional units of the nervous system. 
 
• Every neuron consists of a body (soma) and a number of processes (neurites).
 
• The nervous system determines that it is a highly complex part of an animal that coordinates its actions and sensory information by transmitting signals to and from different parts of its body. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/747dcd667ed7635fe2f6858202b41b5ba08ff2391b854a4967bb8f5636bb8fc7.png] 

 
• The nervous system is the major controlling, regulatory, and communicating system in the body. 
 
• It is the center of all mental activity including thought, learning, and memory. 

__
 
• Together with the endocrine system, the nervous system is responsible for regulating and maintaining homeostasis
 
 
• A neuron is the structural and functional unit of the brain.
 
• The longest cell in the human body is the neuron.
 
• The nervous system consists of the brain, spinal cord, sensory organs, and all of the nerves that connect these organs with the rest of the body. 
 
• Together, these organs are responsible for the control of the body and communication among its parts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Neurons are the basic functional units of the nervous system, and they generate electrical signals called action potentials, which allow them to quickly transmit information over long distances. 
 
• To generate and transmit nerve impulses, support the neurons; may serve a nutritive function and help regulate the chemical environment of the neuron.
 
• The nervous system produces a response on the basis of the stimuli perceived by sensory structures.
